unit.why: A short anecdote about the Maggid of Kozienice on the eve of Yom Kippur: the townspeople weep at his door, he weeps with them, declares himself the greater sinner and rolls in the dust, and then they go to Kol Nidre.

stories.summary_en: On Yom Kippur eve the people of Kozienice come weeping to the Maggid's door for atonement; he weeps with them, says he is a greater sinner than they, rolls in the dust, and they then go to the synagogue for Kol Nidre.

tags.why: The scene takes place on the eve of Yom Kippur, leading to Kol Nidre.

quotes: גם אני יותר פושע מכם והתגולל לעפר
tags.why: The Maggid declares himself more sinful than the people and abases himself.
The anecdote's point is the tzaddik's humility.
The townspeople weep for atonement of their sins on Yom Kippur eve.
The scene ends with everyone going to the synagogue for the Kol Nidre service.
The townspeople come to the tzaddik's door and he receives them.
Women appear only collectively, coming and weeping with the rest of the town.
